articleTitle: A Quantum Phase Neuron
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: A quantum phase neuron (QPN), including its structural design and the derivation of input-output relationships, is proposed for the first time. The research focuses on the design process of quantum phase neurons when the probability amplitude is a real number. The paper provides the corresponding encoding functions based on different input types, which offers the flexibility for handling complex input data patterns. At the same time, the proposed single-layer QPN is used to solve the XNOR logic operation problem, and the superiority of the proposed QPN in performance is shown. The research presented in this paper demonstrates the potential and application prospects of QPN in constructing high-efficient quantum neural networks.

articleTitle: Enhanced Infrared-Visible Image Fusion Method with an ISP Based Degradation Model
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: The performance of infrared (IR) and visible (VIS) image fusion tasks depends on the quality of source images, which are usually impacted by various degradation factors in real-world scenarios, leading to poor quality and visual effects of the fused images. By learning the mapping from low-quality (LQ) source images to high-quality (HQ) fused images, neural networks can remove the impacts of degradation factors, generating HQ fused images. However, the lack of paired LQ source images and corresponding HQ fused images poses a significant challenge in training a fusion network. Considering the effectiveness of the image processing pipeline (ISP) in processing IR and VIS images, reversing specific steps of ISP can accurately simulate the image degradation process. Building upon this research, we propose a novel ISP-based degradation model that reverses several ISP steps while incorporating various degradation factors, thereby generating LQ IR and VIS images from source images to train the fusion network. Experimental results on multiple image fusion datasets demonstrate that our method significantly enhances the quality and visual effects of fused images.

articleTitle: Intelligent Supplier Evaluation and Selection Module for Fast-Moving Consumer Goods
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Since increasing competition and decreasing resources in the globalizing world, companies have focused on activities that add value to the product and supply chain management has become crucial. Thus, the concept of sustainability has emerged as environmental awareness and gained importance as a result of both international and national environmental agreements in order to prevent permanent damage from production activities. In this study, eight criteria extracted from academic studies are taken into account and examined for a green supply chain. These criteria were evaluated by experts working in the fast food sector, which has the highest market share among domestic producers in Turkey. The interval-valued intuitionistic fuzzy analytic hierarchy process method is utilized to determine the selection of the most appropriate strategy for this company from the four green supply chain management strategies (eco-innovation-based management, eco-industrial parks and strategic partnerships, spreading green consumption awareness and green purchasing and distribution).

articleTitle: Enhancing Product Bundling with Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Recommendation systems have become popular in recent years. Today, in a world where competition is increasing, recommendation systems are used in many different areas. When the number of products and customers is high, it is important to recommend the right products to the right people. For this reason, different methods are widely used in recommendation systems and various techniques have been explored and developed to improve recommendation accuracy. The study evaluates the potential use of large language models. ChatGPT is chosen to create and expand existing product bundles. Apriori and word embedding models such as Word2Vec and FastText have been prepared for recommendations based on existing and bundles. The results show that large language models can improve bundle creation processes in some scenarios and that tools such as ChatGPT have the potential to improve recommender systems.

articleTitle: Natural Language Processing in Albanian Language
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: This paper examines the application and challenges of Natural Language Processing (NLP) in the Albanian language, a less-studied computational - linguistic domain. Despite the rapid advancements in NLP technologies, there is a notable lack of research and tools for Albanian, which limits the inclusion of the Albanian-speaking population in the benefits of Artificial Intelligence (AI) advancements. Through a comprehensive review of recent academic papers, this study analyzes the effectiveness of NLP in areas such as hate speech detection, named entity recognition, and news analysis for the Albanian language. The paper emphasizes the importance of developing NLP resources for Albanian to ensure cultural preservation, social inclusion, and technological advancement. It highlights the potential of models like Bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) and Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) in improving the understanding of Albanian text, which is crucial for applications that have a social impact. The findings emphasize the need for continued research and development to encourage an inclusive digital space that respects linguistic diversity and promotes language equality in AI.

articleTitle: Application of the CTPN-CRNN Model with Attention Mechanism in Scene Text Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: With the rapid development of the internet, textual information contained in online images has become a key resource for automated information extraction. However, this information is often embedded in images with complex backgrounds or irregular layouts, posing significant challenges to traditional text recognition methods. This paper proposes a method based on CTPN (Connectionist Text Proposal Network) and attention mechanism-enhanced CRNN (Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network) for extracting key information from online images, effectively supporting information extraction and data analysis tasks. The method first uses CTPN to accurately detect text areas in the image and generate text box candidates, then employs the CRNN enhanced with an attention mechanism for character recognition within the candidate boxes We conducted experimental validation on the ICPR MTWI 2018 dataset, which includes a variety of real-world application scenarios. The results show that the CRNN model combined with CTPN and the attention mechanism outperforms traditional OCR methods on this dataset. The high precision and robustness of this method provide strong technical support for automated information extraction, product data analysis, and intelligent search, offering broad application potential.

articleTitle: A Defect Detection Method for Artificial Leather Based on YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: In recent years, the demand for high-quality artificial leather has increased, highlighting the need for accurate and efficient defect detection methods. To address issues of inefficiency and a high leakage rate m manually inspecting defects in artificial leather, this study introduces a defect detection approach using an enhanced YOLOv5 network. In this method, the Ghost convolution module replaces the CNN convolution module within the CSP structure of the backbone network. This adjustment simplifies the network architecture, enhances model feature extraction comprehensiveness, and reduces the parameter count in the backbone network. Additionally, the SE attention mechanism is incorporated into the backbone network, allowing it to learn the texture and edge features of small target leather defects more effectively and rapidly, thereby improving the network’s sensitivity to minor defects Finally, by substituting the original CIoU loss function with the EIoU loss function, the method intensifies the penalty on discrepancies between the predicted and actual bounding boxes, specifically in width and height. Experimental results indicate that the modified model achieves an overall average accuracy (mAP) of 87.1% on the tested dataset, offering a more efficient solution for detecting defects m artificial leather.

articleTitle: Optimization algorithm for global k-means algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: The k-means method is widely utilized for clustering. Its simplicity, efficacy, and swiftness make it a favored choice among clustering algorithms. It faces the challenge of sensitivity to the initial class center. The enhancement strategy for the k-means algorithm focuses on refining the initial selection of cluster centroids, no longer using its random selection of initial class center points, but starting from the entire dataset, choosing the most distant point to serve as the starting cluster centroid. This can also prevent the local optimization problem of the k-means algorithm. The improved algorithm proposed in this article is an effective method that can select the initial class center point from a global perspective and reduce computation time. The suggested approach has undergone rigorous testing and comparative analysis across multiple datasets, yielding commendable outcomes.

articleTitle: Tensor Decomposition-Based Feature Transfer Learning for BCI Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Event-Related Potential (ERP) detection and enhancement remain significant challenges in EEG signal processing due to the complex and multidimensional nature of ERP signals. This paper addresses these challenges by proposing a novel framework that combines low-rank tensor representation with heuristic feature transfer learning for efficient ERP processing. By leveraging tensor decomposition, we capture intricate multidimensional patterns in ERP data, facilitating the extraction of informative features. These features greatly reduce processing time, making the method particularly suitable for online Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) applications. We also present a feature transfer learning mechanism utilizing tensor decomposition, which facilitates the efficient adaptation of features trained on multiple subjects to new subjects, requiring only a small amount of calibration data. This approach leverages shared classification structures across subjects, allowing for rapid deployment and minimizing the need for extensive retraining. Our results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves reasonable ERP detection accuracy while drastically reducing computational overhead, presenting a robust solution for real-time BCI systems.

articleTitle: Underwater Image Restoration Based on Improved SwinIR Model
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Image restoration is a classic foundational visual task, aimed at recovering damaged images, such as those affected by compression, blurring, or noise, to high-definition clarity. Although current image enhancement techniques largely rely on convolutional neural networks, the efficient capabilities of Transformers demonstrated in complex visual tasks have not yet been extensively applied in the field of image restoration. This paper presents an optimized image restoration strategy based on the SwinlR model, which is applied to the task of underwater image restoration. In the shallow feature extraction phase, deep separable convolution technology is employed; while in the deep feature extraction phase, a Spatial Gated Feedforward Network (SGFN) is utilized. The experimental data suggests that the novel approach surpasses conventional techniques in effectiveness and has effectively minimized both the model's parameter quantity and computational demands.

articleTitle: Research on Mango Ripeness Based on Yolo
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Mangoes are a crucial agricultural crop in southern China, especially in the Guangxi region, where their production significantly contributes to the local economy. However, challenges in ripeness identification lead to quality control issues in storage, transportation, and sales. This research proposes a detection method for mango ripeness based on an improved YOLOv5 model. Traditional fruit ripeness detection methods have certain limitations in terms of accuracy and efficiency. To improve detection accuracy, this research replaces the backbone network of the YOLOv5 model with ResNet50 and introduces the Coordinate Attention (CA) mechanism to enhance the models feature extraction ability and the accuracy of ripeness judgment Experimental results show that the improved model demonstrates higher precision and robustness in detecting mangoes at different stages of ripeness. The research results indicate that the improved YOLOv5 model can effectively identify and distinguish mango ripeness, providing technical support for fruit quality management and harvesting in the agricultural field.

articleTitle: Integrating the dynamic optimization strategies of Adam and AdaGrad
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been a key research area since the 1950s, initially focused on using logic and reasoning to create systems that understand language, control robots, and offer expert advice. With the rise of big data and deep learning, AI has advanced in applications like recommendation systems, image recognition, and machine translation, primarily through optimizing loss functions in deep neural networks to improve accuracy and reduce training time.Gradient descent is the core optimization method but faces challenges like slow convergence and local minima. To overcome these, algorithms like Momentum, AdaGrad, RMSProp, Adadelta, Adam, and Nadam have been developed, introducing momentum and adaptive learning rates to accelerate convergence. This paper presents a new optimization algorithm that combines the strengths of Adam and AdaGrad, offering better adaptability to different learning rates.

articleTitle: A Framework for Solving Quadratic Knapsack Problem Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: The quadratic knapsack problem (QKP) with constraints has been a focus of attention in combinatorial optimization, where traditional exact algorithms face difficulties in solving large-scale problems due to the problem’s NP-hard nature, and heuristic algorithms have difficulty in generating high-quality solutions in effective time. To solve QKP quickly and accurately, this paper proposes a graph pointer network (GPN) framework with hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL). The first stage of the method trains low-level neural network to find feasible solutions that satisfy the constraint as much as possible. The second stage trains the high-level neural network based on the first stage using the objective function as a penalty term. After the HRL, our trained hierarchical GPN (HGPN) model can effectively solve the QKP. In addition, we add a greedy strategy in the decoding process to further improve the solution accuracy of the neural network solver. Experiments show that our proposed method can approximate the optimal solution produced by the Docplex solver and outperforms most end-to-end neural network solvers.

articleTitle: Adaptive Particle Swarm Optimization of U-net Parameters for Marine Aquaculture Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Marine aquaculture image segmentation plays a crucial role in managing aquatic resources and environmental protection. Traditional deep learning models rely on manual parameter tuning for image segmentation, which limits their efficiency and accuracy. This paper proposes an adaptive Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm to optimize the parameters of the U-net model automatically. The algorithm dynamically adjusts the PSO parameters based on the population’s entropy and clustering metrics and employs a hill-climbing algorithm to address the issue of the PSO easily falling into local optima, enhancing the algorithm’s adaptability. The proposed algorithm updates and iterates particles to automatically find suitable model parameters. The remote sensing data used in this experiment were from the Yellow Sea aquaculture area near Dalian, China, with a segmentation accuracy of 91.8%. This method improves segmentation accuracy, reduces the burden of manual parameter tuning, and provides an effective solution for optimizing deep learning models.

articleTitle: Hyperspectral Image Analysis Using Maximum Abundance Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: This paper presents a satellite hyperspectral image processing method that utilizes a maximum abundance classifier to categorize different regions of hyperspectral images into ground truth classes. First, the class names for each endmember and their corresponding columns in the signature matrix are identified, followed by the visualization of their spectral profiles. Abundance maps for the endmembers are then generated using the fully constrained least squares (FCLS) method. Afterward, the maximum abundance classifier is applied, and the resulting classified image is displayed with color-coded pixels. The abundance maps illustrate the spatial distribution of endmembers across the hyperspectral image, where the abundance values of each pixel represent the proportion of each endmember present. By determining the highest abundance value for each pixel and assigning it to the corresponding endmember class, the pixels within the hyperspectral images are classified. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed MAC method effectively handles mixed pixels. In addition, it can effectively deal with the mixed pixel problem in hyperspectral images because it identifies components by calculating the abundance values for each pixel rather than relying solely on single spectral features.

articleTitle: Contrastive Learning Regularization Method for Information Extraction of Floating Raft Aquaculture
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Addressing the challenge of coherent speckle noise in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery, as well as the impact of intra-class variability and inter-class similarities on the performance of raft aquaculture information extraction, this paper proposes a contrastive learning regularized triplet attention (CLRTA) approach. Following feature extraction by the encoder, the triplet attention mechanism is incorporated to filter out the noise and focus on the floating raft regions, thereby enhancing the model’s capability to process information in complex backgrounds. Subsequently, a contrastive learning loss function is introduced to minimize distances within the same category while increasing distances between different categories, thus enhancing the model’s discriminative ability towards intra-class variability and inter-class similarities. Information extraction is conducted in the raft aquaculture areas of Shangchuan Island, Guangdong Province, validating the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Fractional-order Adaptive Sliding Mode Projective Synchronization of Different Hyperjerk Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive fractional order sliding mode projective synchronization scheme for different hyperjerk systems with uncertainty and disturbances. A fractional order sliding mode controller with three fractional terms is proposed for the projective synchronization of different hyperjerk systems. The uncertainty and disturbance is considered with adaptive scheme. Numerical simulation verifies the effectiveness and feasibility of the control method.

articleTitle: Filtered Sliding Mode Tracking Controller for Robot Joint Using Linear Matrix Inequalities Design
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: In this paper, a Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMI) design of a filtered sliding mode controller is proposed, and applied to a robot joint for tracking control. The robot joint dynamics are linearised through the compensation of nonlinear terms (i.e. frictions, gravity, and coriolis torques), and a filtered control action is designed in order to prevent the chattering problem. The optimal control design using LMI technique can then be applied to the combined low pass filter and robot joint system, ensuring the stability of the closed loop. The proposed method is evaluated through numerical simulations of two degrees of freedom (2-DOF) end-effector type therapeutic robot, showing the robustness and performances of the controlled system under tracking task.

articleTitle: Insulators Defect Detection for Power Grid Based on Improved Yolov7 Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: High-current out-of-phase closed bus is an essential link in the transmission of electric energy and is widely used in thermal power stations, hydropower stations and nuclear power plants. Although these busbars have the advantages of excellent dustproof effect and strong magnetic shielding, they are susceptible to insulator aging and damage in long-term operation, posing a potential safety risk to the power grid. Due to the enclosed space inside the bus and the complexity of external maintenance tasks, manual inspection has problems such as inefficiency and low safety. In order to solve these problems, this paper proposes an improved detection algorithm based on Yolov7 for insulator defect detection in hydropower station scenarios. Because of the particularity of Yolov7 network structure and application scenarios, this paper proposes a Channel Feature Enhancement module to enhance the channel representation ability of the network. In addition, an Edge Feature Enhancement module is introduced to improve the boundary detection of insulators by enhancing the contrast between the target and the background. Considering the limitations of existing studies in specific scenarios and the scarcity of dataset, this paper constructs and accurately annotates an insulator defect detection dataset applied to hydropower station scenarios. Experimental results show that the improved-Yolov7-tiny algorithm in this paper achieves a balance between accuracy and inference speed.

articleTitle: WeCAViT: A Weighted CNN model for Pneumonia Detection in Chest X-rays
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Pneumonia is a severe respiratory disease with high global mortality rates, particularly impacting children under 5 and the elderly. Early and accurate detection of pneumonia is critical for improving patient outcomes; however, diagnosing pneumonia through chest X-rays (CXR) is often challenging and requires substantial expertise. This paper presents WeCAViT–a Weighted Ensemble CNN with Attention and Visual Transformer–a novel AI-driven model designed to enhance pneumonia detection in CXR images by automating and improving diagnostic accuracy. The WeCAViT model integrates an ensemble of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), a Spatial and Channel Attention block, and a Visual Transformer (ViT), each contributing uniquely to feature extraction. CNN encoders capture local features at varying scales (24 24 to 112 112), allowing multi-resolution analysis. The attention block highlights the most relevant spatial and channel details, while the Visual Transformer captures broader, global characteristics within the image. Evaluated on the PneumoniaMNIST dataset, WeCAViT achieved a test accuracy of 93.6%, outperforming or matching current state-of-the-art models. These results suggest that WeCAViT could serve as an effective tool in clinical settings, supporting timely and reliable pneumonia diagnosis.

articleTitle: Pseudoinverse Learning Algorithm As a Unified Framework For Normalization In Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: In recent years, several normalization methods have been proposed in order to train neural networks, including batch normalization, layer normalization, weight normalization, and group normalization. However, it does not exist a unified framework which can unify these normalization techniques for easy using to most researchers. In this paper, we proved that most of the normalization methods can be realized in a unified framework, namely PseudoInverse Learning (PIL) algorithm. When training neural network with PIL algorithm, no other normalization methods are needed further since normalization is natural embedded in PIL algorithm. And like normalization techniques, PIL algorithm not only can speed up training deep neural networks, but also can act as a regularizer to improve generalization when utilizing low rank constraint PIL for autoencoders. Hence, our proposed unified framework can help researchers to tackle the difficult of choosing proper normalization methods, and this can greatly facilitate their research process.

articleTitle: Adaptive Prescribed Time Path Following Controller for Underactuated Surface Vessels
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Heading control of marine vehicles is an important issue in navigation and control engineering. This paper investigates the design of a prescribed-time robust adaptive path following control problem of an underactuated surface vessel with parametric uncertainties, unknown disturbances and control input constraints. The establishment of prescribed-time property consists of a prescribed-time regulation of the steering control systems and novel prescribed-time Line of Sight (LOS) guidance control, both of which satisfy the prescribed-time requirement. The feasibility of separate independent control design for the steering and the guidance control systems is guaranteed through the development of new results on nonlinear prescribed-time cascade systems with non-vanishing uncertainties. The Lyapunov method is employed to show that the equilibrium point of the whole system is prescribed-time input to state stable. Numerical simulations are carried out to validate the performance of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Semantic Neuroanatomical Segmentation of Brain MRI Scans Using Pretrained SynthSeg Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Deep 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with trained algorithms have proven the possibility to distinctively partition brain regions to reduce manual division and expert labeling of neuroanatomical structures. Although many machine learning techniques implement this strategy, most can be time-consuming and quite difficult to interpret as contrast modeling with varying resolutions can be obscure upon differentiating across regions. SynthSeg, a 3D U-Net algorithm, contains the ability to segment scans in datasets of multiple modalities and a variety of target domains without the need to retrain as it is trained with preconstructed data derived from a general 3D U-Net model for volumetric segmentation, thus facilitating the analysis of large quantities of bioimaging data in short periods of time. This is made possible due to the randomization technique where the contrast and resolution of the preconstructed training data are selected randomly to increase deep learning performance and accuracy. Due to its ability to learn from fluctuating contrast and resolution types via the randomization technique, its segmentation robustness is maintained across datasets. SynthSeg can learn from pretrained designated labels for characterization of diverse populations to improve detection and diagnoses of a vast array of diseases. Using SynthSeg, a subset of the Child and Adolescent NeuroDevelopment Initiative (CANDI) dataset containing brain MRI volume for a single patient was used with its corresponding ground truth image to analyze and exhibit highly accurate predictive modeling within each scan. The average Dice index across all labels for the MRI volume is 0.80793, which indicates an almost perfect segmentation accuracy.

articleTitle: Improved LYT-Net Image Enhancement Model for Underwater Robotics Vision
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Although underwater robots can replace humans to explore the ocean which is rich in resources but fraught with unknown risks, there are phenomena such as monotonous colors, complex backgrounds and uneven illumination in the underwater environment, which makes it difficult for underwater robots relying on the optical vision system to obtain clear images and is not conducive to subsequent recognition and grasping tasks. In this paper, relevant preparatory work was carried out for underwater image processing applicable to underwater robots, and the underwater imaging model as well as other underwater image processing models were analyzed. Subsequently, a method combining the underwater physical model and the dark channel image was proposed to improve LYT-Net, enabling it to be applicable to mobile embedded devices such as underwater robots. After training and testing on the real datasets LSUI and UIEB, our model achieved good results on important indicators such as PSNR and SSIM. Meanwhile, it met the theoretical requirements of mobile devices in terms of FLOPs, Params and single-frame processing time, which verified its robustness and real-time processing ability in various underwater environments.

articleTitle: A Discrete-Time Collaborative Neurodynamic Approach to Distributed Global Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: In this paper, a discrete-time projection neural network with an adaptive step size (DPNN) is proposed for distributed global optimization. The DPNN is proven to be convergent to a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker point. Several DPNNs are utilized in a collaborative neurodynamic framework for solving distributed global optimization problem. The efficacy of the collaborative neurodynamic approach with DPNNs is demonstrated through simulation results.

articleTitle: TAPNet: Tunnelled Asymmetric Pyramid Network for Achieving a Pragmatic Semantic Segmentation Solution for Autonomous Driving
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Semantic segmentation, vital in autonomous driving, is a pixel-level prediction task that is used to partition images into distinct regions. Effective models must capture multi-scale context to enhance segmentation quality but also need to be computationally efficient for practical deployment on resource-constrained devices. Hence, the challenge is to maximize accuracy and speed while minimizing model complexity to transform semantic segmentation into a successful practical reality. In response, we propose a Tunneled Asymmetric Pyramid Network (TAPNet) that combines short and long-range context with high efficiency. It is based on the TAP module, which extracts multi-scale short-range context in a highly efficient manner. Unlike conventional methods, our feature tunneling technique reinforces feature maps with finer details, enhancing segmentation accuracy. To efficiently capture long-range context, we propose the Pair-wise Aggregated Reinforced Scale-Enlarged Spatial Pyramid Pooling (PARSE-SPP) module, designed for ultra-low computational overhead. Based on the TAP and PARSE-SPP modules, we are able to achieve a high-performing segmentation model that strikes an optimal balance between accuracy and efficiency. This makes TAPNet a strong candidate for autonomous driving in real-time scenarios. More specifically, with only 0.29 million parameters, it achieves 68.75% and 68.6% mIoU on Cityscapes validation and test set, respectively. More interestingly, it achieves 161.55 FPS on a single RTX 3090 card. The related code is available at https://github.com/NadeemAtif-Alig/TAPNet.

articleTitle: Attitude Detection Model Based on Improved High Resolution Network
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: 2D human posture detection, a challenging task in computer vision, aims to identify human body key points and is widely used. The HRNet model performs well in human key point detection. To enhance its effect in human posture detection and address suboptimal prediction accuracy in interactive occlusion, this paper combines HRNet and Transformer. The Transformer's attention mechanism handles complex image dependencies, and HRNet obtains image features. By embedding the Transformer's attention mechanism module into HRNet's backbone network and integrating a self-designed double-branch structure and convolutional attention module an improved HRNet model is constructed. The DConvAttention module processes extracted features and the convolutional attention mechanism balances image frequencies, enhancing processing and discrimination of complex backgrounds and occlusions and improving detection performance. In tests of complex and occluded images, the improved HRNet Local model has a 4.2M parameter increase, 0.5G FLOPs increase, and 1% mAP increase compared to HRNet, with the same recall rate. The improved HRNet Global model has 11M more parameters, 1.1G more FLOPS a similar or slightly higher recall rate, and a 2% higher mAP value.

articleTitle: Invariant Set Analysis and Control Synthesis of Multi-Equilibrium Switched Systems under Control Constraints
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: This paper investigates the problems of invariant set analysis and control synthesis for multi-equilibrium switched systems under control constraints. A control strategy based on the invariant set method is proposed, accompanied by criteria formulated as linear matrix inequalities, ensuring that the state remains within the mode-dependent invariant sets. Furthermore, considering the control constraints in practical scenarios, a multi-equilibrium switched controller with control constraints (MESCC controller) is designed. Compared to existing works, the proposed method incorporates mode-dependent dwell time conditions and mode-dependent invariant sets, thereby offering enhanced design flexibility. An example of an aero-engine control system is presented to demonstrate the effectiveness and potential of the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Target Detection in Hyperspectral Imagery Using Spectral Signature Matching Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: This paper presents a method for detecting a known target (e.g., trees) in hyperspectral images using spectral matching techniques. The pure spectral signature of the target material is used to identify and locate the target within the image. Specifically, we employ the Spectral Angle Mapper (SAM) algorithm for spectral matching to detect the known target (trees). The reference spectrum for the trees is sourced from the ECOSTRESS spectral library and serves as the benchmark for spectral comparison. In this approach, the spectral signatures of each pixel in the hyperspectral data cube are compared with the reference spectrum. Pixels with the closest matching spectral characteristics are classified as part of the target material. An SAM score map is generated for different regions in the test dataset, quantifying the spectral match between each pixel's signature and the reference spectrum. Using a minimum score threshold, regions in the data are classified based on spectral similarity, assigning each pixel a class label according to its match with the reference spectra.The experimental results demonstrate that this thresholding approach successfully localizes target regions, resulting in a commendable mean squared error (MSE) of 0.020492 for tree labels, showcasing the algorithm's reliable detection performance. Furthermore, we compared the Spectral Angle Mapper (SAM) algorithm with other advanced spectral matching algorithms. It was found that the Normalized Spectral Similarity Score (NS3) algorithm achieved the lowest MSE of 0.018992, surpassing both SAM and the Jeffries-Matusita Spectral Angle Mapper (JMSAM).

articleTitle: A Recurrent Neural Network Based Bicriteria Repetitive Motion Collision Avoidance Scheme for Motion Planning of Dual Redundant Manipulators
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: To achieve low joint-angle drift and avoid mutual collision between dual redundant manipulators (DRMs) when they are doing collaboration works, a recurrent neural network based bicriteria repetitive motion collision avoidance (BRMCA) scheme is proposed for motion planning of DRMs. By designing a combined optimization objective encompassing both repetitive motion criterion and collision avoidance criterion, the BRMCA scheme has larger feasible region and less constraint contradiction issues compared with traditional inequality constraints based method. Furthermore, by incorporating velocity-level kinematic model and physical limits of DRMs into the scheme, a time varying quadratic programming (TVQP) problem is formulated. The linear variational inequality-based primal-dual neural network (LVI-PDNN) is used to solve the proposed scheme due to the high accuracy and low computation complexity. Finally, through comparison simulations of tracking Circle-shape and C-shape trajectories between BRMCA scheme and minimum velocity norm (MVN) scheme, it exhibits that the proposed BRMCA scheme can achieve low joint-angle drift, collision avoidance and high tracking accuracy when DRMs are doing cooperative tasks.

articleTitle: A Fully Sparse Detector with Cascade Heads for LiDAR-based 3D Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: LiDAR-based 3D object detection is a critical component of perception systems in autonomous driving. Existing detectors typically rely on dense feature maps for 3D object prediction. However, as the perception range expands, the computational overhead associated with dense feature maps increases quadratically, creating significant challenges for scaling to long-range detection scenarios. To address this issue, fully sparse detectors have recently been proposed, but they often suffer from suboptimal performance or excessively complex architectures. In this paper, we present CHNet, a fully sparse detector designed to overcome these limitations by introducing a cascade head module, which consists of two sequential heads. By generating coarse object predictions, creating new feature points based on centers of the predicted objects, and aggregating features of the entire object to these new center points, CHNet enhances the qualities of object feature representations, achieving higher detection performance. Notably, CHNet effectively addresses the center feature missing problem in LiDAR-based 3D object detection by adding at most a hundred new feature points, offering a potential avenue for future research. On the widely used Waymo Open and Argoverse2 datasets, CHNet achieves impressive results without any additional embellishments.

articleTitle: A Novel LSTM Optimized by Neurodynamic Network for Heat Prediction of Power Equipment
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: With the rapid development of smart grid and substation equipment, the heating problem of power equipment has become an important factor affecting the stability and safety of equipment. The traditional equipment monitoring method has lag, and it is difficult to predict the heating trend of the equipment in time. Therefore, a long short-term memory based on neurodynamic network(NN-LSTM) is proposed to improve the accuracy of predicting the heating trend of power equipment. In this paper, the predictive ability of the LSTM network is improved by combining the neurodynamic optimization strategy. And it is applied to power load forecasting and transformer oil temperature forecasting. Experimental results show that NN-LSTM is superior to the traditional LSTM model on the two datasets, the mean square error is effectively reduced, and the prediction accuracy is higher.

articleTitle: Decentralized Federated Learning with Auto-switchable Local Optimizers
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel decentralized learning algorithm over networks, termed as DLAGD, which combines the consensus mechanism with an auto-switchable local optimizer. Specifically, each node updates its local model parameter based on either gradient descent algorithm or Adam-like algorithm, which depends on a local switching function. Such switchable local optimizer can better capture the structure information of local loss function than existing algorithms relying on a fixed local optimizer, then has the potential to accelerate the convergence rate and improve the generalization performance. We theoretically prove that DLAGD can converge to the neighborhood of a stationary point at a sublinear rate for non-convex problems. Finally, numerical experiments are presented to show the superior performance of DLAGD in terms of the training rate and test accuracy.

articleTitle: Multi-OP: A Multilevel Model for Orbital Prediction Using Multi-Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: To address the increasing computational demands and the need for enhanced stability in the orbit prediction of large-scale resident space objects (RSOs), this paper proposes a novel method grounded in orbital dynamics, which defines and computes environmental, dynamical, and fingerprint features. A feature fusion strategy is then applied to introduce a Multi-OP model comprising a shared backbone and a prediction layer tailored for orbit prediction tasks. Specifically, the shared backbone integrates environmental and dynamical features to capture public information, thereby enhancing the model’s generalization ability. The prediction layer, in contrast, leverages fingerprint features to generate individualized orbit predictions for each RSO. Experimental results demonstrate that the Multi-OP model not only enhances the accuracy of orbit prediction but also exhibits remarkable stability.

articleTitle: A hybrid intelligent control strategy to improve the stability of wind-PV-thermal-bundled system
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: This paper investigates the intelligent optimal control problem for the stability of wind-PV-thermal-bundled (W-PTB) system. Based on the weak damping characteristics of the WPTB system, the damping ratio, bus voltage, and generator active power are constructed as objective functions, and an improved greater cane rat algorithm (IGCRA) is proposed for the parameter optimization problems of power system stabilizers (PSS), power oscillatory damping (POD) controller, and unified power flow controllers (UPFC). Compared with the existing methods, the algorithm proposed in this paper improves the optimization and global search capability and prevents local optimization by introducing the Sin chaos model, nonlinear control, and the Cauchy mutation operator. Finally, different states of the WPTB system are simulated separately, and the results show that the method proposed in this paper can give full play to the advantages of each controller, significantly enhance the system damping ratio, and shorten the amplitude of the oscillations and suppression of low-frequency oscillations (LFO) occurring in the system.

articleTitle: Cross-Organization Single-cell RNA-seq Data Clustering Methods
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Single-cell transcriptome sequencing technology provides a new way to understand cell heterogeneity and functional diversity. Batch effect correction and clustering are important steps in cross-tissue single-cell transcriptome data analysis. Choosing the right method has a great impact on downstream analysis such as cross-tissue cell type identification. First, this paper describes five typical batch effect correction methods and nine single-cell clustering methods, and analyzes their advantages and disadvantages. Then, a comparative experimental analysis is conducted on the mouse single-cell transcriptome atlas dataset Tabula Mûris. The performance comparison experiments and analysis of cross-tissue single-cell transcriptome data batch effect correction methods and clustering methods are performed using evaluation indicators such as accuracy, adjusted Rand index, normalized mutual information, and Davidson-Bourdin index. The experimental results show that among the batch effect correction methods, the clustering performance after ComBat batch effect correction is the best, and the accuracy, adjusted Rand index, normalized mutual information, and Davidson-Bourdin index after clustering have obvious advantages over other batch effect correction methods. Among the clustering methods, scDCC and scCCL have the best overall performance in terms of accuracy, adjusted Rand index, normalized mutual information, and Davidson-Bourdin index, with balanced performance and short time consumption.

articleTitle: Tomato Leaf Disease Identification and Growth Dataset Augmentation Based on UAE-GAN
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: To delve into the characterization of growth disorders in different crops, it is important to support the model with a large amount of image data that includes a variety of disease types and disease levels to capture the typical and subtle differences of various diseases on plant leaves. However, the actual process of gathering data is challenging, sample coverage is challenging to accomplish, data capture is impeded, and the quality of the data is subpar. This work aims to address the issue of data shortages by employing technical methods. In particular, we creatively investigated the UAE-GAN approach, which naturally combines CycleGAN, U-Net, Variational Autoencoder VAE, and Autoencoder to increase the data. Among these, U-Net can precisely extract the small details of disease locations in crop photos and provide a strong basis for further processing thanks to its special codec architectural benefits. The Variational Autoencoder (VAE) significantly enhances the diversity of data by mapping the image to the latent space and sampling based on a certain probability distribution, so producing new image samples that are distinct from the original image yet inherently connected. Learning the coding and decoding of the original image is the foundation of autoencoders. If a mild disruption is introduced into the coding process, it can achieve data augmentation in another dimension and create a sequence of new images with just little modifications to the original image. The aforementioned models are closely linked with CycleGAN to efficiently map and convert in a variety of picture domains and to fully leverage CycleGAN's remarkable unsupervised image conversion capabilities. The perception ability, feature capture ability, and information conversion ability of the fusion model for crop image data are significantly improved, and the key elements of each link in the data enhancement process are comprehensively considered to ensure that the generated new image data can not only retain the key features of the original data but also effectively extend the data boundaries to satisfy the requirements of model training for richness and diversity. On this basis, tomato leaf image data enhancement is studied, and the performance and stability of the combined model are verified.

Author Keywords: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation

articleTitle: A Neurodynamic Approach for Distributed Optimization with Delayed Feedback
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: In this paper, a neurodynamic approach with communication delay is proposed for the sake of solving distributed optimization problems. First, the relationship between the equilibrium of the algorithm and the optimal solution of the distributed optimization problem is established. Then, sufficient conditions for the equilibrium to converge to the optimal solution of the optimization problem are provided in the form of linear matrix inequalities, in the case of communication delay. In addition, numerical simulation verifies the validity of the neurodynamic approach with communication time delay.

articleTitle: Clustering Algorithm for Vessel Trajectory Anomaly Detection Based on Binary Hashing Method
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Timely identification of abnormal ships through trajectories make daily commercial trade transportation safer. However, current methods for identifying abnormal ships through vessel trajectories have issues such as high time cost and high sensitivity to parameters. To address such issues efficiently, a clustering method based on hashing algorithm applying Long Short-Term Memory neural networks is proposed to capture abnormal local and temporal information in trajectories. The trajectories are converted into hash codes that present thier characteristics succinctly. Then, the dominant set clustering method that does not require setting hyperparameters is used to cluster and find abnomal trajectories according to similarity relationship computed by corresponding hash codes. The proposed method is validated on a dataset of real vessel trajectories, which basically achieves the identification of abnormal vessel trajectories with lower time cost compared to other methods.

articleTitle: Research on Collaborative Filtering Algorithm of E-commerce Based on Flink
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: In online shopping, a person’s interest in a product is closely related to whether they will purchase it Analyzing people’s interest in various products on time, along with product recommendations, can increase purchase rates. However, in many cases, We only know user implicit feedback, such as browsing or favoriting items, and cannot directly access user explicit feedback, such as product ratings. Moreover, users have limited exposure to products, resulting in a sparse user-item matrix. The traditional Alternating Least Squares (ALS) algorithm can partially address the is of of matrix sparsity but its accuracy in recommending products based on implicit feedback alone is insufficient. This paper proposes an improved ALS algorithm that converts implicit feedback into explicit ratings. We calculate the browsing frequency of a product based on user browsing counts. For a given product, we represent user preference by suimming the browsing frequencies of all products with browsing frequencies less than or equal to that of the product. Then, by multiplying the preference level by the product’s maximum rating, we derive a product rating, achieving a transformation from implicit feedback to explicit scores. Additionally, traditional collaborative filtering algorithms often use offline data, which may not align with user current preferences. To improve the algorithm’s accuracy, we also utilize Flink for real-time data processing, allowing us to capture the most recent feedback data. This study tests the approach using the UserBehavior dataset from the publicly available Tianchi dataset. Experimental results indicate improvements in both Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE).

articleTitle: Automated Motion System of 5-DOF Hybrid Serial-Parallel Manipulator for Invasive Medical Procedures
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: In the medical profession where accuracy is vitally critical, operations are increasingly adopting robotic technology to eliminate mistakes and improve precision. Current robotic-assisted surgical systems are sometimes limited in their usefulness in complex procedures because they lack real-time haptic feedback and adaptive motion control, despite improvements in the field. A 5-DOF hybrid serial-parallel manipulator is presented in this study, which has been developed to enhance dexterity, motion stability, and real-time force feedback in a range of minimally surgery applications. During surgical procedures, the device enhances precision and control by combining AI-assisted motion correction with a haptic glove-controlled master-slave mechanism. Increased trajectory stability, reduced force application errors, and greater surgical precision are all demonstrated by simulations and experimental validation in MATLAB Simulink. The findings indicate that adaptive AI and enhanced haptic feedback can significantly improve robotic-assisted procedures, making them more effective and reliable for a range of minimally invasive surgeries. In the future, the focus will be on improving response time, making the system more adaptive, and integrating it into the actual environment.

articleTitle: Portfolio Optimization and Risk Assessment Based on Random Weighting, Markowitz Mean-variance Model and Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: This paper explores the portfolio optimization and risk assessment problem by exploiting the random weighting method, Markowitz mean-variance model, and genetic algorithm. First, the historical K-line data provided by the official documents of Baostock is obtained and cleaned, and the normalized processing results of the trading day and closing price are given. Then, the selected stocks are analyzed in detail through the visual analysis of the return rate data, the calculation of the covariance matrix and correlation coefficient matrix heat map, and the average annual return rate and annual volatility of the stock return rate. Next, three different portfolio optimization methods are used to compare their expected returns, volatility, and weight distribution. Finally, the efficient frontier and capital market line of the portfolio are plotted to evaluate the effects of different methods. In this study, the random weighting method, Markowitz mean-variance model, and genetic algorithm are considered as optimization methods to comprehensively analyze the volatility and risk of the selected stock portfolio. This provides a comprehensive and scientific reference for investors to choose stock investment strategies.

articleTitle: MSAFNet: Integrating Multi-Scale and Self-Adaptive Attention for Comprehensive Feature Representation
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Fine-grained visual classification (FGVC) is a challenging problem in computer vision, focused on distinguishing visually similar subcategories within broader categories. This paper introduces MSAFNet, an innovative framework that integrates two modules: Multi-Scale Attention with Boost and Suppress (MABS) and Self-Adaptive Feature Integration (SAFI). The MABS module enhances discriminative features while suppressing overly prominent ones, ensuring the network learns from a broader range of complementary regions. The SAFI module further integrates local and non-local features, optimizing feature representation for improved classification. We evaluated our approach using three benchmark datasets: CUB-200-2011, Stanford Cars, and FGVC-Aircraft. Experimental results demonstrate that MSAFNet achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing methods by efficiently capturing and integrating multi-scale discriminative information. These improvements are attributed to our novel use of attention mechanisms and adaptive feature fusion to enhance fine-grained feature learning.

articleTitle: Bi-clustering of Binary Data via Neurodynamics-driven Binary Matrix Factorization
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Bi-clustering, also known as co-clustering, is a powerful data analysis technique that simultaneously clusters rows and columns of a data matrix, revealing hidden patterns. In this paper, we propose a neurodynamics-driven binary matrix factorization approach for bi-clustering binary data. The proposed method utilizes multiple discrete Hopfield networks operating concurrently to explore local optimal solutions. Furthermore, a particle swarm optimization rule is iteratively applied to reinitialize the neuronal states for directing the search toward better solutions. Comparative evaluations across six benchmark datasets reveal that the proposed method outperforms five existing methods in terms of five internal and external indices.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Fusion and Saliency Suppression Network for Fine-Grained Visual Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Fine-grained visual classification (FGVC) relies on accurately capturing subtle differences within similar categories, making it a challenging task in computer vision. Current methods often enhance classification by focusing on salient regions or by fusing multi-level features, but they encounter two main issues: (1) excessive reliance on the most prominent regions while overlooking other informative areas, and (2) limited flexibility in integrating features across different scales. To address these challenges, we propose the Multi-Scale Fusion and Saliency Suppression Network (MSFSN), a framework comprising two core modules that can be seamlessly integrated into convolution neural networks. First, we introduce a Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Module (MSFFM) that performs cross-scale feature integration to better capture contextual semantics and fine details. Second, we implement an Attention Suppression Module (ASM) to downplay the most salient features, encouraging the model to explore other potential discriminative regions. Our method does not require additional annotations, such as bounding boxes or key-points, and is designed for end-to-end training. Experimental evaluations on multiple fine-grained benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance.

articleTitle: Neural Dynamics Incorporated Noise-Resistance Bi-criteria Scheme for Redundant Manipulators
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Traditional control schemes of the redundant manipulator are usually difficult to satisfy the needs of many aspects, such as trajectory accuracy, direction tracking, joint physical constraints, noise tolerance, and so on. To solve these problems, from the perspective of optimization, this paper proposes a noise-resistance bi-criteria control scheme and designs an online solution model of neural dynamics (ND). The virtual simulations using the Franka Emika Panda manipulator demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the ND model. Besides, the ND model obtained from the proposed scheme verifies their superiorities in a noisy environment.

articleTitle: Quantifying Bird Strikes due to Migration from a Machine Learning Perspective
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Bird Strikes have always been a persistent threat to the aviation industry. Bird strikes occur when a bird at flight accidentally collides with an aircraft. Such collisions, be it a major or minor ones; often cause catastrophic structural damages and financial losses to both the aircraft and the aviation sector. From the earliest days of aircrafts, birds have always been a source of risk due to the common means of locomotion. Hence, this calls for nuanced approaches and strategies for mitigation of such incidents. Although there exist solutions that have real-time applications, it is important to note that none of these solutions are eco-friendly and environmentally sustainable. Adding to that, there is no solution that considers the correlation factor between migration and such incidents. Additionally, it was observed that out of 442 unique species in bird strike incidents through the dataset acquired for this study, 369 species were migratory leading to a conclusion that majority of the species involved in such incidents are migratory. Therefore, going to the depths of this issue to help prevent bird strikes while proactively working is more important rather than focusing solely on reactive mitigation strategies that are mostly taken post the detection of bird activity. Thus, through this focused study, a thorough understanding of correlation between bird strikes and migration has been established by utilizing the eBird migration data sourced from Cornell Lab of Ornithology and the bird strike data from Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). By leveraging an ensemble of models like Random Forest (RF), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) and Support Vector Machines (SVM), migratory months for all the species were predicted. A correlation of about 53% was achieved between bird strike incidents and migration cycles. This conclusion can be used to ensure better safety measures at the airports prior to flight scheduling and many more other applications.

articleTitle: Efficient and Accurate Two-Step Sequence-Based Loop Closure Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Loop closure detection is a critical issue in Visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (VSLAM), as it involves determining when a robot revisits previously explored locations. To improve the accuracy and real-time performance of loop closure detection, this paper proposes a two-step loop closure detection method based on keyframe sequences. It dynamically partitions the keyframes into sequences based on the angular difference between adjacent keyframes. Sequence-to-sequence matching is performed using the Bag-of-Words (BoW) model. To reduce the time overhead of loop closure detection, we use histograms during the frame-to-frame matching process. This allows us to avoid spending too much time on the extraction and matching of complex descriptors in matched keyframe sequences, while ensuring the accuracy of the results. To further enhance efficiency, we design a filtering mechanism based on past loop closure results and sequence length, which avoids unnecessary detection in frames where loop closures are unlikely to occur. We integrate the proposed loop closure detection approach into VINS-Mono and evaluate it using public datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that our loop closure detection approach outperforms the original approach in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency, making it well suited for real-time large-scale VSLAM applications.

articleTitle: Does Federated Learning Improve the Resiliency of Machine Learning Models Against Data Fault Attacks?
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used in various fields, making it vulnerable to cyberattacks like label-flipping attacks, which alter training data labels to mislead models. This paper evaluates the impact of such attacks on popular ML models, including Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), using two datasets. Results show that while RF is most resistant, MLP performs best under normal conditions but suffers greatly under attack. To mitigate this, we propose a federated learning (FL) approach that distributes training across multiple servers, enhancing robustness. Our results on the Breast Cancer Wisconsin dataset demonstrate FL’s effectiveness, achieving no accuracy drop with 20 servers, a training time of 99.79 seconds, and 3.82 MB bandwidth usage. FL proves highly resilient, making it suitable for critical applications like medical diagnosis in adversarial environments.

articleTitle: Target Identification and Detection Using Hyperpectral Signature Transformation
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Hyperspectral imaging has emerged as a powerful technique for target detection and material identification across various fields, from remote sensing to environmental monitoring. This paper proposes a spectral signature matching method for detecting a known target (i.e., sea water) in hyperspectral images. By analyzing pixel-by-pixel spectral characteristics, spectral matching algorithm computes the similarity between the spectral signature of each pixel and that of known target materials.The proposed method employs the Jasper Ridge hyperspectral data from an urban landscape to demonstrate the algorithm’s effectiveness, with results revealing high accuracy in target detection even in heterogeneous environments where various land cover types (like water, vegetation, urban structures, soil, and rocks) are intermixed within the same area. This highlights the algorithm’s robustness in discerning similar spectral features. The experimental results demonstrate that the Jeffries-Matusita Spectral Angle Mapper (JMSAM) outperformed the Spectral Angle Mapper (SAM) and the Normalized Spectral Similarity Score (NS3) algorithms, by achieving the lowest MSE of 0.056933.

articleTitle: Classifying Land Cover Using Hyperspectral Image and LiDAR Data
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: This paper proposes an advanced approach to land cover classification by integrating hyperspectral and LiDAR data to leverage their complementary strengths. Hyperspectral sensors capture detailed reflectance across numerous spectral bands, providing unique spectral signatures that differentiate various land cover types. On the other hand, LiDAR technology offers high-resolution elevation data, enabling accurate characterization of surface structures. This paper details the process of converting unorganized LiDAR point clouds into organized formats for effective analysis, followed by a robust data fusion technique that combines spectral and spatial information. Utilizing a land cover classification methodology on the MUUFL Gulfport dataset, collected in November 2010, we evaluate the effectiveness of our approach by comparing classification accuracies of multiple machine learning algorithms, including kernel classification model, support vector machines, and others. Our results demonstrate significant improvements in classification accuracy when hyperspectral and LiDAR data are fused, highlighting the efficacy of this integrated methodology for complex land cover analysis.

articleTitle: High-Precision Face Generation and Manipulation Guided by Text, Sketch, and Mask
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Recently, diffusion models have made remarkable progress in face image processing using more modality. We propose a novel framework for high-precision face generation and manipulation guided by text, sketch, and mask input. Our approach introduces a Dual Branch Diffusion Model that integrates residuals into the diffusion process, transforming the standard denoising diffusion model into a unified, interpretable model suitable for both image generation and manipulation tasks. Quantitative results show that our method achieves competitive performance across multiple metrics and excels in preserving identity features, manipulating local regions, and performing structured edits. Ablation studies further reveal the effectiveness of the Dual Branch and Latent Space Regularization in enhancing the quality and diversity of generated images while emphasizing the necessity of balancing these components under different task settings.

articleTitle: Motion-Force Control for Redundant Robots With Orientation Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: In the realm of industrial automation, the control of redundant robots is essential, particularly in precision manufacturing. Traditional dynamics-based methods often face challenges in handling the complexity of redundant degrees of freedom in robots. This paper introduces an innovative approach to motion-force control utilizing joint velocity commands based on kinematic analysis, representing a shift from traditional dynamics-based methods. The problem of motion and force control is organized into a constrained quadratic programming(QP) scheme by integrating desired forces, predefined trajectories, and orientation maintenance. A recurrent neural network (RNN) is presented to achieve redundant robot kinematic control. The proposed scheme achieves accurate hybrid control of force and position, which is confirmed by simulation results. This approach has the potential to enhance the efficiency and precision of industrial automation systems.

articleTitle: IRSEnet: Differentially Private Image Generation with Multi-Scale Feature Extraction and Residual Channel Attention
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Privacy-preserving image generation is particularly crucial in fields like healthcare, where data are both sensitive and limited. However, effective privacy preservation often compromises the visual quality and utility of the generated images due to privacy budget constraints. To address this issue, in this paper, We propose a novel network architecture, IRSEnet, which combines multi-scale feature extraction technology and residual channel attention mechanisms, aiming to enhance the visual quality of generated images and improve the performance of downstream classification tasks under differential privacy. The differential privacy mechanism ensures the security of sensitive data during training, while the multi-scale feature extraction module enhances feature extraction capabilities through parallel convolutional layers at multiple scales. Additionally, the channel attention module dynamically adjusts channel weights to focus on the most discriminative features. Experimental results demonstrate that this model significantly improves the utility of generated images and the accuracy of downstream classification tasks while preserving privacy. Future work will explore the application of this approach on larger datasets and across more diverse tasks.

articleTitle: Imbalanced Data Classification Using Transfer Learning and Oversampling
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: A common challenge when applying transfer learning to specific domains is imbalanced datasets, where some classes have significantly fewer samples than others. This can skew the model's predictions toward the majority class. In this paper, we aim to investigate the effectiveness of oversampling methods including random oversampling technique and image augmentation in hyperspectral image classification, exploring their potential to enhance performance.This paper proposes an oversampling method which are applied on the imbalanced datasets by randomly duplicating samples from the minority classes until the number of samples matches that of the majority classes. In addition, image augmentation techniques (rotation, flipping, zooming) are conducted to increase the diversity of the minority class. Moreover, the training process of the proposed ResNet-18 transfer learning network is fine-tuned with optimized parameters to address challenges like overfitting and underfitting. Furthermore, the proposed transfer learning model's adaptability and robustness are evaluated and compared with the other two state-of-the-art transfer learning models, GoogLeNet and AlexNet. The experimental results show that the GoogLeNet model achieves impressively higher classification accuracy than the other state-of-the-art models for imbalanced and balanced Flowers dataset (93.61% and 93.89%, respectively), while the proposed ResNet-18 model obtains the highest accuracy for imbalanced and balanced Food dataset (87.63% and 89.69%, respectively). In addition, all transfer learning models are able to obtain higher accuracy on the balanced data than on the imbalanced data.

articleTitle: A Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring Method Based on Relative Position Matrix and Residual Network
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
abstract: Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) technology identifies various appliances’ types and operational status by analyzing electrical data collected from sensors in residential or commercial buildings, offering significant practical value. However, due to the limitations of existing methods for constructing appliance features, the identification performance of NILM models needs improvement. Addressing this, we propose a method for constructing appliance features based on a relative position matrix (RPM), which more accurately captures the temporal characteristics of electrical data compared to other methods. Additionally, a deep learning model based on the improved ResNet18 with multi-scale fusion is proposed for the load identification task. In this paper, comparative experiments were conducted on the PLAID dataset. We compared the RPM with three appliance feature construction methods: voltage-current trajectory (VI), markov transition field (MTF), and gramian angular field (GAF). We also compared our results with advanced methods reported in other literature. The results show that this method outperforms existing methods in terms of precision, recall, and F1 score across various evaluation metrics.

articleTitle: ICICIP 2025 Cover Page
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Control and Information Processing (ICICIP)
